behavioral_notes.observation: The jsonrpc POST /website_links/new is the link-builder's create endpoint: it rejects empty url ({'error':'empty_url'}) then calls link.tracker.search_or_create([post]).read() with the post dict carrying url + optional label/campaign_id/medium_id/source_id (UTM ids resolved client-side via the WebsiteLinksTagsWrapper find_or_create_record). search_or_create (in the parent link_tracker module) validates/normalizes the URL, back-fills defaults, builds a dedup key over LINK_TRACKER_UNIQUE_FIELDS and either returns the existing matching tracker or creates a new one -- so creating the 'same' URL+UTM combo twice yields the same short link rather than a duplicate. The returned read() dict (short_url, short_url_host, code, count, ...) is what the OWL UI renders. This find-or-create / dedup semantics is invisible to metadata.

/website_links/recent_links proxies link.tracker.recent_links(filter, limit) which search_reads trackers ordered by one of three filters: 'newest' (create_date DESC), 'most-clicked' (count!=0, count DESC) or 'recently-used' (count!=0, write_date DESC); an unknown filter returns {'Error':...}. The 'count' field is link.tracker's stored/aggregated click count computed from link.tracker.click rows, so the recent-links panel surfaces live click statistics per link. The per-link stats page route /r/<code>+ renders website_links.graphs from code.link_id.read()[0], feeding the WebsiteLinksCharts OWL interaction (all-time/last-month/last-week clicks + per-country pie charts).

behavioral_notes.element: Short-code redirect dependency on link_tracker (/r/<code>) + WebsiteUrl.statistics_shorten_url (/r/<code>+)
behavioral_notes.observation: website_links itself does NOT own the click-recording redirect: the public route /r/<string:code> lives in the parent link_tracker controller and on each hit calls link.tracker.click.sudo().add_click(code, ...) (geoip country, UTM context) then redirects (get_url_from_code -> redirected_url). website_links only adds the authenticated /r/<code>+ statistics page (and /r, the builder landing page rendering website_links.page_shorten_url). Thus the short link's value chain spans two modules: link_tracker = capture+redirect, website_links = the website UI to mint links and read their stats. The '+' suffix on the route is the convention separating a redirect (/r/CODE) from its stats view (/r/CODE+).

/website_links/add_code lets a designer rename a link's short code: it resolves the existing link via the init_code's link.tracker.code, then creates a new link.tracker.code row (UNIQUE(code) constraint) pointing at the same link_id unless that code already exists for the link. A link can therefore carry multiple short codes all resolving to one destination. Driven from the WebsiteLinksCodeEditor public.interaction on the stats page.

website_links overrides _compute_short_url_host so the short-URL host is the *current website's* base URL (website.get_current_website()) when it matches the company's website_id, else the company base URL -- making generated /r/ links multi-website aware rather than using the raw system base_url. action_visit_page_statistics returns an act_url to short_url + '+' (new window), the backend hook into the same stats page.

The whole link-builder UX is client-side: 5 JS files, 2 XML templates, one OWL component (WebsiteLinksTagsWrapper, the UTM campaign/medium/source autocomplete-and-create selector) and three public.interactions (WebsiteLinks = the create form + recent-links list, WebsiteLinksCharts = Chart.js clicks/countries graphs, WebsiteLinksCodeEditor = inline short-code rename). A website.assets_editor service registers the 'Link Tracker' custom menu (website_custom_menus:website_links.menu_link_tracker). Routes return JSON/read() dicts and QWeb shells; the interactive builder, clipboard copy, notifications and charts exist only in static/src -- entirely outside Python model metadata.

software_services: /website_links/new (jsonrpc: create-or-find a tracked short link from url + UTM ids)
/website_links/recent_links (jsonrpc: list links by newest / most-clicked / recently-used with click counts)
/website_links/add_code (jsonrpc: add an alternate short code to a link)

link.tracker.code -> link.tracker (alternate short codes, ondelete cascade)
link.tracker.click -> link.tracker (click events, source of 'count' stats)
link.tracker.click -> utm.campaign (related, stored for campaign click aggregation)

side-effect: POST /website_links/new -> link.tracker.search_or_create -> find-or-create tracker (dedup on url+UTM) -> read() back to OWL UI
side-effect: public GET /r/<code> (owned by link_tracker) -> link.tracker.click.add_click (geoip country, UTM) -> redirect to destination URL
flow: /website_links/recent_links + /r/<code>+ read link.tracker 'count' aggregated from link.tracker.click rows -> click/country charts
side-effect: /website_links/add_code -> new link.tracker.code row (UNIQUE code) reusing one link_id

classification.apqc_category: 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services
classification.rationale: website_links is a mediating-technology (Stabell & Fjeldstad value network) layer for marketing-link distribution: it provisions short /r/<code> links that mediate between a campaign and an open population of recipients/visitors, linking the two parties and capturing each contact (click) for attribution. Its worth grows with the number of links shared and the audience reached -- the network signature -- rather than a sequential transformation (chain) or a diagnostic problem-solving cycle (shop). activity_class is primary because minting and operating the tracked-link channel (the create/redirect/measure service the website UI delivers) is the value the module exists to produce, not a back-office support function. apqc_category 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services because the artifact is campaign reach/attribution tooling -- UTM-tagged trackable links to measure marketing-channel effectiveness and feed campaign click stats -- squarely demand-side marketing measurement. Note utm (the reference-data mixin) is classed support, but website_links is the public-facing operational tool that distributes and measures the links, hence primary here.

standard_capabilities: self-service website page (/r) to generate short trackable URLs with UTM campaign/source/medium
find-or-create dedup so the same url+UTM yields one stable short link
click capture + redirect via /r/<code> (geoip country, UTM context)
recent-links panel with newest / most-clicked / recently-used filters and live click counts
per-link statistics page (/r/<code>+) with all-time/month/week click and per-country charts
custom / alternate short codes per link
typical_fits: marketers minting tracked links for campaigns, ads and social posts
attributing inbound traffic to a campaign/source/medium for reporting
sharing branded short links and reading click/geography stats
feeding utm.campaign click_count from distributed links
common_gaps: no built-in QR-code, A/B link rotation, or expiry/scheduling of links
click analytics limited to count + country/time-window (no device/referrer breakdown out of box)
designer-group gated -- no portal/public self-service link creation for non-staff
no native integration to external URL shorteners or GA event push (UTM params only)
bot/duplicate-click filtering and unique-visitor metrics not provided
